title: Government equity stakes and critical-minerals deals: who was positioned to profit
summary: The core of the lead is documented. A June 28, 2026 NYT investigation (Lipton and Sonne) counted at least 14 critical-minerals companies tied to the Trump or Lutnick families that had received or were seeking more than $8.9B in federal support (mostly commitments and letters of interest), and Senate Democrats built July 2026 letters on it. The strongest instances are 1789/Vulcan, Dominari/American Ventures via Skyline-Kaz Resources (with Cantor raising $210M for a project partner), and Cantor as lead placement agent on USA Rare Earth's $1.5B PIPE alongside a $1.6B Commerce LOI. The Cantor-TMC and Cantor-Critical Metals links are also real. But MP Materials, Lithium Americas and Intel are not on the reported list and no family tie to them was found. Family gains are largely unquantified, and no evidence shows influence; Commerce, the White House, Cantor and the Trump family deny wrongdoing. Audit update: Trump's own accounts bought Intel shares in early 2026 after the government stake (AP, May 2026), a personal-portfolio link rather than a family firm in the deal; Cantor's role in American Ocean Minerals' >$150M placement is documented, while ties for Energy Fuels, Titan and Guardian Metal remain unverified.

sub_claims.statement: Reporting (NYT) found Trump-family or Lutnick-family-linked firms held positions in, or advised, a dozen-plus critical-minerals companies that received or sought federal backing.
sub_claims.finding: Confirmed as reporting. A New York Times investigation by Eric Lipton and Paul Sonne (published 2026-06-28, syndicated by the Boston Globe) counted at least 14 companies with financial ties to the Trump or Lutnick families. The government had provided, or was considering providing, more than $8.9B in support to them, and some had permit applications before Commerce. Secondary coverage gives the 14 as Kaz Resources, USA Rare Earth, Perpetua Resources, ASP Isotopes, Critical Metals, Vulcan Elements, The Metals Company, Trilogy Metals, American Ocean Minerals, Guardian Metal Resources, Titan Mining, Westwater Resources, ReElement/American Resources Corp. and Energy Fuels. The Times reported that Cantor Fitzgerald, now run by Lutnick's sons, frequently served as adviser, underwriter or placement agent. On 2026-07-30/31, Sens. Blumenthal, Schiff and Warren cited the $8.9B and 14-deal figures in letters to DoD, DOE, Commerce, Interior and EXIM, plus a separate letter to OSC on Vulcan. The $8.9B is mostly commitments, letters of interest and conditional loans, not disbursed money.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 Capital (Don Jr.) invested in Vulcan Elements before its federal loan and equity package.
sub_claims.finding: This is covered in C26 and not repeated in full here. 1789 joined Vulcan's $65M Series A in August 2025. On 2025-11-03 a $1.4B package followed, including a $620M OSC conditional loan, $50M in Commerce CHIPS money and government warrants/equity. ProPublica reported that White House aide Peter Navarro initiated the deal. 1789 and Don Jr. deny any role, and no reporting shows foreknowledge.

sub_claims.statement: Dominari / American Ventures (Trump sons) took a position via Skyline Builders in the Cove Kaz / Kaz Resources tungsten project backed by U.S. financing, and Cantor also profited.
sub_claims.finding: This is covered in C47. The FT (May 2026) and NYT (June 2026) reported that the sons bought into Skyline in August 2025 through a Dominari-linked SPV. That was before Tokayev reportedly told Trump on 2025-09-22 that Cove Kaz would get the project, and before the deal was signed on 2025-11-06. Skyline then took 20% of Kaz Resources, which holds non-binding EXIM (up to $900M) and DFC (about $700M) letters of interest. In May 2026 Cove sought about $400M more from OSC. The NYT also reported that Brandon and Kyle Lutnick's Cantor Fitzgerald helped raise $210M for one of the project's investment partners, potentially earning millions in fees; the partner's identity and the fee amount were not available in the coverage accessible here. SEC filings do not name the brothers, the FT found no evidence of foreknowledge or influence, and a Trump family lawyer called the NYT report 'libelous'.

sub_claims.statement: Cantor Fitzgerald was banker on USA Rare Earth's private raise alongside the Commerce Department's equity-and-loan deal.
sub_claims.finding: On 2026-01-26 USA Rare Earth announced a non-binding Commerce CHIPS letter of intent for about $1.6B: $277M in federal funding and a $1.3B senior secured loan. The government would receive 16.1M shares and about 17.6M warrants, roughly 10% (8-16% depending on warrant exercise). The LOI had no price floor. The same day USAR announced a $1.5B common-stock PIPE at $21.50 a share, anchored by Inflection Point. Cantor Fitzgerald, chaired by Brandon Lutnick, was lead placement agent and Moelis was co-agent. USAR said Cantor was not involved in the government transaction. On 2026-02-26 Warren, Wyden and Van Hollen wrote to Lutnick, also alleging that billionaire Trump allies got access to PIPE shares. That is an allegation, and the specific investors are not confirmed here. Commerce reportedly did not answer by the 2026-03-11 deadline. Cantor's fee is not public in the sources found.

sub_claims.statement: The Metals Company, a Cantor client, sought deep-sea mining permits from NOAA, which sits under Lutnick's Commerce Department.
sub_claims.finding: Cantor Fitzgerald is reported as one of TMC's leading bankers and financial advisers. TMC said in March 2025 it would seek U.S. licences, filed its applications under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act within about a week of Trump's April 2025 seabed-mining executive order, and refiled under NOAA's streamlined rules in January 2026. NOAA certified an exploration application, the first since Trump took office, and Earthjustice and conservation groups sued in 2026. No commercial recovery permit had been reported issued. Whether Lutnick recused himself from TMC matters was not established. This is a permit, not money, so it presumably counts toward the 14 but not the $8.9B.

sub_claims.statement: Cantor holds a position in Critical Metals Corp (Tanbreez, Greenland), a company the administration discussed taking a stake in.
sub_claims.finding: The Deep Dive reports that Cantor Fitzgerald is among Critical Metals' largest investors. The current stake size was not found, and Cantor's holdings partly reflect its brokerage and research role; Cantor initiated coverage with a Speculative Buy and an $18 target on 2026-07-14. Reuters reported in October 2025 that administration officials discussed taking a stake in Critical Metals. No completed U.S. equity stake was found. The company raised its Tanbreez ownership to 92.5% in April 2026. CRML is on the NYT list of 14.

sub_claims.statement: Perpetua Resources, ASP Isotopes and Westwater, all on the NYT list, have Cantor ties and federal support.
sub_claims.finding: Perpetua: EXIM advanced a large loan in May 2026 for the Stibnite gold-antimony project. Figures differ between $2.7B and $2.9B against an earlier $2.0B application. Cantor's documented role in the accessible sources is analyst coverage (Buy, target $27); any banking role is per the NYT only. ASP Isotopes: Cantor was a joint book-runner on its June 2025 $50M offering and covers it at Overweight. The specific federal support counted for ASP was not identified in accessible sources. Westwater: received EXIM financing for its graphite project in August 2026; the Cantor or family tie was not identified. Audit additions on the four less-covered names: American Ocean Minerals: Cantor Fitzgerald (chaired by Brandon Lutnick) and Citigroup arranged a private placement of more than $150M tied to its April 2026 merger with Odyssey Marine and act as its capital-markets advisers (Reuters, documented in C77); the federal action is a NOAA seabed permit review, advanced in July 2026. Energy Fuels: the federal action is documented, a conditional OSC/Pentagon loan of about $725M for rare-earth expansion announced in June 2026, but no Trump- or Lutnick-family tie was found in accessible coverage beyond its inclusion on the NYT list. Titan Mining: received EXIM financing for its Empire State Mines zinc-graphite expansion (about $15.8M per Mining.com; one commentary says $21M), but no family tie was found. Guardian Metal Resources: a commentary source reports about $6.2M in Defense Department study money for a Nevada tungsten site; neither that nor a family tie was confirmed. For Energy Fuels, Titan and Guardian the nature of the NYT-reported tie remains unverified here.

sub_claims.statement: The administration's equity stakes in MP Materials, Lithium Americas, Trilogy Metals and Intel are among the deals where Trump- or Lutnick-linked firms were positioned to profit.
sub_claims.finding: The government actions are real. In July 2025 the DoD bought $400M of MP Materials convertible preferred stock (conversion at $30.03, about 15%, making it the largest shareholder), plus warrants, a 10-year $110/kg NdPr price floor and offtake, and a planned $150M loan. In October 2025 DOE took warrants for about 5% of Lithium Americas plus 5% of the Thacker Pass JV with GM when restructuring its $2.26B loan (a $435M drawdown and $182M of deferred repayments). On 2025-08-22 the government agreed to take 433.3M Intel shares (9.9%) for $8.9B at $20.47 a share, funded from unpaid CHIPS ($5.7B) and Secure Enclave ($3.2B) grants, plus a conditional 5% warrant; the stake is passive. On 2025-10-06 the government took about 10% of Trilogy Metals for $35.6M, with warrants that could lift it to about 17.5%, alongside Ambler Road permits; Trilogy shares roughly tripled. But MP Materials, Lithium Americas and Intel do not appear on the NYT list of 14 as reported, and this research found no reported Trump- or Lutnick-family position in them. Trilogy is on the NYT list, but the nature of its family tie could not be confirmed from accessible sources. Treat the brief's grouping of these stakes with the conflicted deals as unsubstantiated except for Trilogy. The MP, Lithium Americas and Intel terms are stated from widely reported 2025 deal announcements and were not re-sourced in this pass. Audit addition: one Trump-family position in Intel has since been reported. AP (2026-05-19) reported that Trump's own first-quarter 2026 periodic transaction report showed Intel purchases (one secondary source dates one to 2 March 2026), months after the government took its stake; a Trump spokesperson said third-party managers have 'sole and exclusive' authority over the portfolio. This is a post-stake portfolio holding by Trump himself, not a family firm positioned in the deal, and no MP Materials or Lithium Americas holding by the family was found.

sub_claims.statement: Family-linked firms made documented gains from the government actions.
sub_claims.finding: Gains are mostly unquantified. Cantor earned placement fees on the $1.5B USAR PIPE and reportedly on the $210M Kaz-related raise, but the amounts are not public. 1789's Vulcan stake and the sons' Skyline/Kaz position are unrealized and private or thinly traded. No realized family profit tied to a specific government action is documented. The share-price jumps on announcement (Trilogy, USAR) benefited all holders, including the government.

sub_claims.statement: Family members or Lutnick influenced the federal decisions.
sub_claims.finding: No document shows a Trump son or Lutnick son lobbying for any of these awards. The closest is ProPublica's report that Navarro initiated the Vulcan deal (C26). Commerce says neither Lutnick nor anyone at the department 'has interacted with or had any discussions whatsoever with Cantor Fitzgerald' about rare-earth companies. Congressional letters (Feb 2026 House Natural Resources; Feb 2026 Warren/Wyden/Van Hollen; Jul 2026 Blumenthal/Schiff/Warren) and CREW FOIA requests seek records. Post-midterm coverage (Nov 2026) says Democrats plan formal investigations, but no finding exists yet.

corrections: The brief groups MP Materials, Lithium Americas and Intel with the family-linked deals; the NYT list of 14 as reported does not include them and no family-firm position was found. The one later link is Trump's personal portfolio buying Intel shares in Q1 2026, after the government stake (AP, 2026-05-19).
'Around a dozen-plus' is the NYT's 'at least 14' companies; the $8.9B is support provided or under consideration (LOIs, conditional loans, warrants), not money disbursed.
USA Rare Earth's federal package is a non-binding LOI ($277M funding plus $1.3B loan for ~10% equity), with no price floor; Cantor's role was the parallel $1.5B private PIPE, not the government deal.
Kaz Resources' $1.6B is non-binding EXIM and DFC letters of interest; the Trump sons' stake is indirect, via a Skyline SPV, and not named in SEC filings.
The Metals Company's connection is a NOAA permit process, not federal funding.
denials_and_context: White House spokesman Kush Desai: 'the only special interest guiding the Trump administration's decision-making is the best interest of the American people.'

Commerce: neither Lutnick nor anyone at the department 'has interacted with or had any discussions whatsoever with Cantor Fitzgerald' regarding the rare-earth companies. Lutnick says he divested Cantor; critics note his stake went to trusts and adult sons who run the firm.
Cantor says it merely serves as a partner for companies raising capital in critical minerals; USA Rare Earth said Cantor was not involved in the government transaction.
1789 Capital and Don Jr. deny any role in the Vulcan loan (C26); a Trump family lawyer called the NYT Kaz report 'libelous' and demanded a retraction (C47).

Context cutting the other way: the administration has done many mineral deals (one tally is about 160 deals and $40B), so overlap with a dominant critical-minerals banker such as Cantor is partly structural. The national-security rationale for reducing China dependence is bipartisan.

Source limits: direct fetches of NYT/Boston Globe, CNBC, Senate sites and most outlets were blocked in this session, and the web-search budget ran out before MP Materials, Lithium Americas, Intel, Energy Fuels, Titan, Guardian and American Ocean Minerals could be checked individually. Those items rely on search-result summaries.
